messages.subject: centered stick-breaking transform & inverse
parts:
Silly me. I forgot that I'd added Jacobians to
the auto-dif class:

void jacobian(std::vector<var>& dependents,
std::vector<var>& independents,
std::vector<std::vector<double> >& jacobian);

So I could use that to test the Jacobian of
the transform in a nice self-contained unit test
which is now in transform_test.cpp.

And it works. The code's pretty simple now. Here's
the centered constraining transform, where

-- y is the unconstrained K-1 vector
-- x is the K-simplex,
-- lp is the log probability, to which the function adds the
log Jacobian determinant of the transform (in *******-ed line)


template <typename T>
Matrix<T,Dynamic,1>
simplex_constrain2(const Matrix<T,Dynamic,1>& y,
T& lp) {

using stan::math::logit;
using stan::math::inv_logit;
using stan::math::log1p_exp;
using stan::math::log1m;

int Km1 = y.size(); // K = Km1 + 1
Matrix<T,Dynamic,1> x(Km1 + 1);
T stick_len(1.0);
for (int k = 0; k < Km1; ++k) {
double eq_share = -log(Km1 - k); // = logit(1.0/(Km1 + 1 - k));
T y_k_plus_eq_share(y(k) + eq_share);
T adj_y_k(y_k_plus_eq_share);
T z_k(inv_logit(adj_y_k));
x(k) = stick_len * z_k;
lp -= log1p_exp(y_k_plus_eq_share) + log1p_exp(adj_y_k); // **********
stick_len -= x(k); // equivalently *= (1 - z_k);
}
x(Km1) = stick_len; // no Jacobian contrib for last dim
return x;
}

The total cost in expensive ops to do a transform is:

(K-1) log()
(K-1) auto-dif var allocations
(K-1) inv_logit()
2(K-1) log1p_exp()

I think it should be pretty numerically stable, but please
look it over and let me know if you see problems.

Here's the inverse function,

template <typename T>
Matrix<T,Dynamic,1>
simplex_free2(const Matrix<T,Dynamic,1>& x) {

using stan::math::logit;

stan::math::check_simplex("stan::prob::simplex_free(%1%)", x, "x");

int Km1 = x.size() - 1;
Matrix<T,Dynamic,1> y(Km1);
T stick_len(x(Km1));
for (int k = Km1; --k >= 0; ) {
stick_len += x(k);
T z_k(x(k) / stick_len);
y(k) = logit(z_k) + log(Km1 - k); // - logit(1.0 / (Km1 + 1 - k));
}
return y;
}

For the same reason I'd like to add a

bernoulli_inv_logit(x|alpha)

= bernoulli(x|inv_logit(alpha))

it might be nice to use the constraining transform above to
define

categorical_stick_breaking(x|alpha)

= categorical(x|simplex_constrain(alpha))

or the more intuitive op for direct calcs,

categorical_soft_max(x|alpha)

= categorical(x|soft_max(alpha))
